:::{#exr-matrix-size-practice}
#### Counting the rows and columns of a matrix

Data with one [row](#def-matrix-row) per observation
and one [column](#def-matrix-column) per measured quantity
is stored as a [matrix](#def-matrix),
so the matrix's number of rows is the number of observations
and its number of columns is the number of quantities.
Let

$$
\matr{C} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 7 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Find $m$ and $n$ such that $\matr{C}$ is an $m \times n$ matrix.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

In @def-matrix, $m$ counts the [row](#def-matrix-row)s and $n$ counts the [column](#def-matrix-column)s.

:::
